messages:
Ava (eng-arch): Quick follow-up from the RFC — we need to finalize the execution-lanes approach (fastpath vs batch-tiling) for the console query layer. Ownership + incremental slimdown plan please.
Mateo (eng-runtime): +1. High-level tradeoff: fastpath preserves low latency but duplicates auth checks and client-facing guards; tiling centralizes RBAC and aggregation but amplifies p99 under tail loads.
Priya (eng-auth): What were the canary perf numbers again? We need concrete baselines to set guard rails.
Ava (eng-arch): Canary snapshot (small synthetic, region-us):
```
fastpath: p50 12ms, p95 38ms, p99 120ms
tiling:   p50 45ms, p95 120ms, p99 450ms
```
Jules (sre): Those tiling p99s are scary for multi-tenant bursts (esp when we get large metric aggregations).
Mateo (eng-runtime): Proposal: incremental slimdown. Keep fastpath for low-compute routes and auth-cache-friendly tokens. Route heavy aggregations to tiling slowpath. Make this route-level policy pluggable.
Priya (eng-auth): How do we avoid RBAC duplication across lanes? Duplicating full auth logic in fastpath increases maintenance and divergence risk.
Ava (eng-arch): Plan sketch: keep canonical auth decision in the control-plane auth service. Fastpath will consult authz on cache miss; add a local LRU/TTL token+perm cache to avoid sync call on hot tokens. Tiling will fetch a compact allow-list per request fanout and validate locally.
Jules (sre): Cache invalidation concerns — role changes must propagate. Propose TTL 30s + event-driven invalidation on role/permission updates.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout job created for "exec-lanes-slimdown" — tomorrow 03:00 UTC :rocket:
Mateo (eng-runtime): Rollout plan: feature-flagged, traffic ramps: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Perf guards: p95 <= 2x baseline, p99 <= 3x baseline, error-rate delta < 0.5%. Automatic rollback if violated.
Priya (eng-auth): Dashboard requirements: auth-cache hit-rate, fastpath fallback rate, per-route p95/p99, auth-service latency and error rate. Need alerts for cache-thrashing and auth-service SLO violations.
Ava (eng-arch): I'll draft the RFC follow-up and a small playbook. Owners: Ava (coord), Mateo (runtime), Priya (authz), Jules (sre). Can we get sign-off on these owners?
Jules (sre): I approve provided we add a tenant-circuit for noisy tenants — short-circuit heavy tenants to dedicated queue/backpressure.
Priya (eng-auth): Add migration checklist: token cache schema, backfill allow-lists for tiling, integration tests for cache rollovers, audit events on cache decisions.
Ava (eng-arch): Noted. Also: audit log policy — emit decision events on cache miss and on enforced fallback to tiling so product teams can trace behavior.
Mateo (eng-runtime): I'll prepare a small shim for route-level config and a toggle to force-tiling per-route for testing.
Ava (eng-arch): Next sync in ~24h. I'll post the draft RFC follow-up and dashboard wireframe. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Mateo (eng-runtime): copying these notes into the architecture docs repo: https://go/repo/arch/console-exec-lanes (will link PR in the draft).
Priya (eng-auth): one last ask — ensure audit logs include whether a decision came from cache vs control-plane. Important for compliance.
Ava (eng-arch): Good call. We'll include that field and the cache-timestamp in the event. Closing now, ping me for anything urgent.
